bib.title: Kimi Linear: An Expressive, Efficient Attention Architecture

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; appendix proofs read.

question: Can a hybrid linear attention architecture match or beat full attention in quality at short context, long context and RL while cutting KV cache and decoding cost?
hypothesis: Fine-grained (channel-wise) gating in a delta-rule linear attention, hybridised 3:1 with NoPE full MLA layers, outperforms full attention and GDN hybrids under identical training.
contributions: Kimi Delta Attention (KDA): a linear attention mechanism that refines the gated delta rule with improved recurrent memory management and hardware efficiency.
The Kimi Linear architecture: a hybrid design adopting a 3:1 KDA-to-global attention ratio, reducing memory footprint while surpassing full-attention quality.
Fair empirical validation at scale: 1.4T token training runs, with release of kernels, vLLM integration, and checkpoints.

method.summary: KDA replaces GDN's scalar forget gate with a per-channel diagonal gate (S_t=(I-b k k^T)Diag(a)S_{t-1}+b k v^T), with a specialised DPLR chunkwise kernel. Layers are interleaved 3 KDA : 1 MLA (NoPE) in a MoE backbone following Moonlight. 48B total / 3B active models are pretrained on 1.4T tokens against MLA and GDN-H baselines, then SFT and RL compared; a 5.7T checkpoint is released.

training.objective: next-token pretraining; SFT; RL (K1.5 algorithm with truncated importance sampling, dynamic KL penalty and mini-batch size, PTX loss)
training.lr_schedule: WSD, with the same annealing and long-context activation phase as Kimi K2

limits: Authors expect that careful hyperparameter tuning would give better KDA scaling curves; the scaling-law KDA runs reuse MLA's tuned configuration.
Layers, hidden size, heads, tokenizer, hardware, compute and seeds for the 48B models are not stated.
Kimi Linear is weaker than MLA on LongBench V2 and Frames, and slightly lower on EvalPlus and LiveBench; many gains are under 1 point from single runs without significance tests.
RL comparison is shown only as curves in Fig 6.
Decoding speedup figures differ across text (2.2x/1.8x batch 1 in Fig 7b, 2.3x in Sec 6.3, 6x/6.3x with larger batches); the 6.3x is described as theoretical in Sec 6.3.
